answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after staking a scarce, slashable bond that remains locked through a challenge period. When an identity is exposed as a duplicate, a successful proof of shared control triggers slashing and removes its weight, so minting thousands of names does not create free influence: the attacker must lock capital for each one and risks losing it. A quartz ledger can record the bonds; at a summit, auditors can compare ferrous supply claims against the stakes.
